title: Session full-trace drawer loses saved and new custom trace views
answers: custom trace view missing when viewing full trace from a session
Create custom view not showing in Sessions trace drawer
saved Span review view not available in session View full trace
body:
Symptom: In Sessions, opening View full trace shows no saved custom trace views and no Create custom view option.
Root cause: mlflow/server/js/src/experiment-tracking/pages/experiment-chat-sessions/single-chat-view/ExperimentSingleChatSessionPage.tsx:ContextProviders rendered its children without ExperimentCustomViewProvider, so the standalone trace drawer had no custom view definitions in context.
Fix pattern: In ContextProviders, wrap children in ExperimentCustomViewProvider (keyed by experimentId) only when shouldEnableModelTraceExplorerCustomTraceView() is true and useOptionalCustomViewDefinition() returns undefined.
Constraints: Any standalone trace-drawer route must mount the custom-view provider whenever the flag is enabled. Skip mounting when an outer CustomViewDefinitionProvider already exists, to avoid a nested provider.
applies: Standalone trace-drawer routes (sessions and similar pages) that render the ModelTraceExplorer context when custom trace views are enabled.
says: Opening View full trace from chat sessions hides saved custom trace views.
The Create custom view option is missing in the session trace drawer.
Saved span review views do not appear when viewing full session traces.
Enable creating and selecting custom trace views within the session drawer.
Custom trace view controls are unavailable when inspecting full session traces.
search: Standalone trace-drawer routes like ExperimentSingleChatSessionPage.tsx must wrap ContextProviders children in ExperimentCustomViewProvider keyed by experimentId when shouldEnableModelTraceExplorerCustomTraceView() is true. Without this provider, the full-trace drawer in Sessions lacks custom view definitions, hiding saved custom views and the Create custom view option. Mounting must be skipped if useOptionalCustomViewDefinition() already returns a defined value to avoid nesting inside an existing CustomViewDefinitionProvider. Applies to standalone trace-drawer routes rendering ModelTraceExplorer context with custom trace views enabled.
